targetTest: starts no knowledge invocation, builds no corpus, and the knowledge index step names the budget
expected: with the run's cost row overrun (negative cost cap) the knowledge pass builds no corpus manifest, starts no invocation, and ends absent with reason budget_exhausted and a detail naming the missing cost cap
actual: the fake knowledge host was not called (the reservation refuses a spent cost row), but the pass had already built an uncapped corpus and written its manifest: 'no corpus manifest was written' failed with true !== false, because the NaN chunk limit removed the corpus cap
semanticAssessment: The target ran and failed on its own assertion that no corpus was built, after the trigger-overrun setup completed and the onboarding reached the knowledge pass (a first version of the test, committed earlier in cf1e41d, failed for the wrong reason: its row update ran before the budget rows existed, so the cap was the contract's 0.2 USD; it is replaced here by a trigger that overruns the row as it is created). The companion unit test fails separately on knowledgeChunkLimit(-0.1) being NaN, not 0. Not a load, fixture or parse fault: the other five tests of the file pass.
